import os

import pytest


@pytest.mark.postgres
def test_invoices_table_exists():
    psycopg = pytest.importorskip("psycopg")
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://ledgerline:ledgerline@localhost/ledgerline_test")) as conn:
        assert conn.execute("SELECT to_regclass('invoices')").fetchone()[0] == "invoices"

I added `src/db.py` with `get_conn()`. It opens a psycopg connection from `DATABASE_URL` and raises `KeyError` if that variable isn't set. I haven't run it or the tests.

It connects with `prepare_threshold=None`. A stored project memory says production and staging go through a transaction-mode pooler on port 6432, and server-side prepared statements fail there with "prepared statement does not exist". Locally, docker-compose talks to Postgres directly, so the problem would only show up after deploy. A comment in the code explains this.

The memory also says to keep transactions short and not to hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. That applies to callers of `get_conn()`.
